Renesas is hiring a Product Assurance Manager to help lead quality execution for its rapidly growing Module business within the Performance Core Power group. This role is being created to address the increasing complexity of our module manufacturing footprint, and will serve as the primary connective tissue between our customers, our external manufacturing partners, and our internal teams to ensure that every module we ship meets the quality bar our customers expect, on time.  You will own the customer-facing negotiation of quality and manufacturing specifications, translating customer requirements into clear, actionable standards that can be executed across our manufacturing flows. You will then work directly with our external manufacturing partners and ODMs to assess, qualify, and continuously monitor their quality systems and processes, ensuring they are capable of meeting the specifications agreed upon with our customers.  When quality issues arise, you will act as the quarterback for resolution — driving root-cause analysis, pulling in cross-functional teams (design, test, product, applications, manufacturing, supply chain, and customer-facing teams) as needed, and ensuring corrective and preventive actions are implemented quickly and effectively. This is a highly cross-functional, externally facing role for someone who is comfortable owning outcomes without owning every function involved in delivering them.  Success in this role will be measured by on-time, quality delivery of products to customers, speed and effectiveness of quality issue resolution, and the strength and reliability of our external manufacturing partners' quality systems.   Key Responsibilities:    Serve as the primary point of contact with external customers to negotiate and finalize quality and manufacturing specifications for module products.  Partner with external manufacturing partners and ODMs to evaluate, qualify, and continuously monitor their quality processes and standards against agreed customer specifications.  Act as the quarterback for quality issue resolution — leading root-cause analysis and pulling in cross-functional teams (engineering, manufacturing, test, supply chain, and customer teams) as needed to drive rapid containment and closure.  Own on-time, quality delivery of finished products to customers, proactively identifying and escalating risks before they impact schedule or quality.  Translate customer-specific quality requirements into clear specifications and drive their adoption across manufacturing partners and internal teams.  Track and report quality metrics and open issues to internal leadership and customer QA teams, ensuring alignment and transparency on status.  Drive corrective and preventive action (CAPA) plans to closure with external partners, verifying effectiveness before issues are considered resolved.  Support structured problem-solving methodologies (e.g., 8D, DMAIC) across partners and internal teams to build durable, repeatable quality processes.  Build strong working relationships with customer quality organizations and external manufacturing partners to enable fast, collaborative resolution of issues.     10+ years of experience in any one of a broad set of roles including quality engineering, product assurance, or manufacturing in the factory.  Bachelor's degree in electrical engineering, materials science, or a related technical field.  Strong communication and relationship-management skills, with demonstrated ability to negotiate specifications directly with customers.  Experience working with external manufacturing partners, contract manufacturers, or ODMs on quality processes and standards.  Working knowledge of root-cause analysis and structured problem-solving methodologies (e.g., 8D, 5-Why, DMAIC).  Ability to lead cross-functional teams through complex, time-sensitive quality issues without direct authority over all functions involved.  Comfort operating in a fast-paced, ambiguous environment as part of a newly created role supporting a growing product line.  Strong experience with semiconductor or module manufacturing flows, especially SMT, and supply chain dynamics is required. We are seeking a motivated Cloud DevOps and AI Security Engineer to help support, secure, and scale our emerging AI infrastructure and development pipeline. Security Monitoring: Review logs, alerts, system activity, and pipeline outputs to help identify, document, and escalate potential vulnerabilities or unusual behavior.  Cloud Infrastructure Support: Assist in provisioning, configuring, and maintaining core AWS services such as VPC, EC2, S3, IAM, Lambda, Docker, and Kubernetes.  Infrastructure as Code: Learn, update, and write basic Terraform, Serverless, or AWS CloudFormation templates under guidance from senior team members.  Access Management: Help manage user permissions and access controls using AWS IAM and least-privilege principles.  Team Collaboration: Work with developers, QA, and operations team members to troubleshoot issues, document findings, and support safe releases for customer-facing web platforms.  Deployment Support: Help maintain and improve automated CI/CD pipelines to support safe, reliable, and repeatable software delivery.  Documentation: Create and maintain clear technical documentation for architecture diagrams, deployment processes, access controls, and security protocols. Cloud Security Fundamentals: Basic familiarity with least privilege, access controls, encryption, secrets management, logging, and secure configuration practices.  Security Monitoring and Triage: Ability to review logs, alerts, system activity, and pipeline outputs, document findings clearly, and escalate potential risks.  Automation Exposure: Basic experience with scripting languages such as Python or Bash to automate repetitive operational or security-related tasks.  Version Control: Familiarity with Git workflows, Bitbucket pipelines, pull requests, branching strategies, and change tracking.  AI-Assisted Engineering: Awareness of how AI coding assistants and automation tools can be used responsibly, including protecting sensitive information, validating tool outputs, documenting AI-assisted changes, and following approved safe-use practices.    Preferred Qualifications    Experience: 0–2 years of experience in IT support, systems administration, cloud operations, cybersecurity, software engineering, web operations, or a junior DevOps role. Education    Degree in Computer Science, Cybersecurity, Software Engineering, Information Systems, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience. Job Summary    This role is responsible for leading MLCC/ inductor/ Embedded substrate strategic sourcing and commercial management, driving cost optimization, ensuring supply continuity, and owning end-to-end supplier strategy. The role requires strong leadership, program management, and cross-functional influence to align business, engineering, and supply chain objectives while driving long-term value creation.    Key Responsibilities    Lead commercial negotiations including pricing, LTAs, capacity agreements, price adjustments, and payment terms for MLCC/inductors/ Embedded substrates.    Own supplier strategy for MLCC/ inductor/ Embedded substrate commodities, acting as a key decision driver in supplier selection and allocation.    Drive cost optimization initiatives using structured methodologies such as cost breakdown analysis, should-cost modeling, and localization strategies.    Lead cross-functional engagement with Engineering and Product Groups to ensure component readiness and alignment across NPI, ramp-up, and lifecycle management.    Ensure supply continuity and resilience by proactively managing capacity planning, allocation strategies, and long-term supply assurance with key component suppliers.    Identify, assess, and mitigate supply chain risks including capacity constraints, geopolitical exposure, cost volatility, and supplier dependency within the passive/component supply base.    Lead contract governance including MSA, NDA, pricing frameworks, and commercial agreements, ensuring alignment with business strategy.    Drive supplier performance management through structured reviews, KPI tracking, and continuous improvement initiatives.    Lead escalation of management and resolution of critical issues related to quality, delivery, capacity, and commercial disputes.    Act as a strategic interface between internal functions (Engineering, Product Group, Supply Chain, and Finance teams) and MLCC / inductor / substrate suppliers to ensure alignment on roadmap, cost, and execution priorities.        10+  years of purchasing/procurement experience, preferably in the semiconductor or electronics industry.    Fluent in English is required; Japanese language proficiency is a plus.    Hands-on experience or strong familiarity with passive components (MLCC/ inductors/ Embedded substrate) is a strong advantage.    Advanced Excel and data analysis skills; proficient in PowerPoint for executive-level presentations.    Strong stakeholder management, communication, and negotiation skills with the ability to influence cross-functional teams and senior stakeholders.    Experience in strategic sourcing, supplier management, or program management is highly preferred. As a Sr. Staff Marketing Manager for Physical AI & Humanoid Robotic Solutions, you will develop and execute the marketing and positioning strategy for Renesas's integrated solutions across the robotics segment in the South East China region. Your responsibility is to position Renesas as the essential semiconductor partner for companies building production-scale humanoid robots by crafting compelling narratives, value propositions, and technical messaging through solution architecture documentation, customer engagement materials, and strategic storytelling. You will need to understand the specific technical requirements of humanoid design: real-time motion control, multi-axis coordination, safety-critical failsafes, deterministic latency, sensor fusion, and power constraints—and create content that articulates how Renesas's full-stack architecture (compute, motor control, analog mixed-signal, sensing, and safety) solves these challenges. You will be the voice translating customer requirements into Renesas marketing narratives and ensuring sales enablement, analyst positioning, and market narrative are synchronized. Your deep technical knowledge, marketing acumen, and entrepreneurial mindset will directly drive how humanoid platform companies of all sizes understand and adopt Renesas's integrated solutions.   Conduct deep market and technical discovery into humanoid robotics challenges and customer requirements. Understand bipedal/quadrupedal motion control, dexterous manipulation, real-time sensor fusion, multi-threaded safety-critical computation, analog signal conditioning, power budgeting, thermal management, and deterministic latency budgets. Translate these into compelling use cases and positioning narratives.  Develop and communicate Renesas's integrated solutions portfolio for humanoid robotics. Create compelling narratives that articulate how compute platforms, real-time safety-critical control, motor control silicon, analog/mixed-signal solutions for power and sensing, and distributed sensing architecture converge into a defensible, reproducible platform vs. point solutions from competitors.  Architect customer-facing solutions and reference designs that map Renesas portfolio to specific humanoid design challenges. Co-develop technical documentation, system architecture diagrams, bill-of-materials, and proof-of-concept roadmaps that de-risk adoption and accelerate design-in timelines.  Create comprehensive solutions marketing content: technical briefs, solution overviews, case studies, white papers, webinar content, presentation decks, and video narratives that position Renesas capabilities for humanoid platform architects and system engineers. Ensure all content is technically accurate, customer-centric, and differentiated vs. competitors.  Develop customer engagement strategies and workshop agendas for humanoid companies. Create discussion frameworks that help customers understand how Renesas solutions map to their specific architecture decisions and long-term platform roadmaps.  Train and enable field sales and FAE teams with technical positioning, competitive messaging, and customer-centric narratives. Develop sales collateral, competitive positioning guides, and talking points that empower teams to articulate Renesas's full-stack advantage in customer conversations. We are seeking an experienced System Architect to define and drive end-to-end architectures for energy generation, storage, power conversion and grid-connected energy systems. The successful candidate will combine strong expertise in power electronics, energy infrastructure and power distribution architectures with the ability to work independently and translate market requirements into scalable technical solutions.  Working closely with customers, SSM, SST and Product Groups, the architect will define system architectures, develop reference solutions and support strategic Energy opportunities from concept definition through proof-of-concept and customer adoption.  This role bridges energy market requirements with Renesas semiconductor and power electronic technologies to deliver next-generation energy infrastructure solutions supporting the transition to a more sustainable energy ecosystem.   System Architecture Design    Define complete energy system architectures including grid connection and protection schemes (MV/LV).  Architect AC/DC and DC/DC power conversion systems including PFC, LLC, PSFB and bidirectional topologies.  Define Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS), BMS architectures and microgrid solutions.  Design distributed energy systems integrating solar PV, wind, fuel cells and renewable sources.  Define architectures for distribution automation, substation monitoring, protection systems, power quality and DER integration.  Ensure compliance with grid codes, safety and reliability requirements.    Power Conversion & Distribution    Translate customer and market requirements into scalable system architectures and reference solutions.  Architect bidirectional energy flows for charging/discharging storage systems and integrating them into local grids.  Optimize system-level efficiency, power density, thermal performance and lifetime reliability.  Support development of solid-state transformer-based systems for high-efficiency energy transfer.    Strategic & Cross-functional    Provide  system requirement documents (SRDs), reference designs, and evaluation platforms  for energy applications.  Collaborate with  utility operators, renewable developers, and storage OEMs  to co-develop innovative power systems.  Track  emerging standards, grid codes, and sustainability regulations  across key markets.  Guide  internal product teams, power IC designers, controls engineers, and thermal/mechanical experts  to build fully integrated solutions.  Contribute to  technical roadmaps and strategic positioning  in energy generation and storage markets.  Support customer engagements and technical workshops to capture application requirements and emerging market trends.  Collaborate with internal marketing, product management and engineering teams to align solution architectures with business objectives, technical constraints and development plans.  Engage with  universities, startups, and consortia  on next-generation power and energy technologies. Demonstrated ability to lead architecture activities independently with minimal supervision.  Deep expertise in:  AC/DC and DC/DC power topologies (PFC, LLC, PSFB, bidirectional)  MV/LV power distribution architectures and protection  Battery energy storage systems (BESS) and battery management  Knowledge of grid codes, interconnection standards, and renewable Power semiconductor technologies (SiC, GaN, IGBT and MOSFET based systems)  Digital power control and energy management algorithms  Protection, metering and power quality solutions integration requirements.  Experience in system-level modeling/simulation (PLECS, SPICE, MATLAB/Simulink, CFD).    Strong  stakeholder alignment and cross-functional communication skill   Strong verbal and written English communication skills (minimum B2, preferably C1) required to work effectively with global teams, customers, and stakeholders    Nice to Have    Experience with  energy metering, smart grid communication protocols (Modbus, IEC 61850, OCPP). You will have a direct impact on implementing and tailoring our enterprise-level customers with innovative and configurable solutions that span both cloud and on-premises infrastructures. You will collaborate closely with key internal and external stakeholders, providing fundamental knowledge of Altium Enterprise solutions that can be transferable to our customers' existing environment and consequently achieving their main business goals and ongoing success. You will play an essential role in bridging the gaps between Sales, Professional Consulting, Software Engineering, Enterprise Deployment, Customer Success, and the R&D organizations.      Responsibilities     Solutions Architecture : Implementing Altium Enterprise solutions by understanding and analyzing our customers existing framework, environment, challenges, and bottlenecks of their electronics hardware development process.   Product Expertise : Provide a deep understanding of Altium’s products, with knowledge of how to apply them in relevant customer contexts. Keep up-to-date on releases, features and product roadmaps.   Technical Guidance : Work closely with our customers to identify, prioritize and quantify key-business drivers, and provide technical expertise on process and optimizations using Altium’s solutions to meet customer objectives and create value.   Statement of Work (SOW) Creation : Developing an agreed SOW where key tasks and deliverables are quantified for each proposed solution and presented to the customer.   Software Engineering:  Collaborate closely with software engineers to develop customized solutions to further accommodate our customers requirements.   R&D:  Work with R&D to resolve software issues that have the highest impact to the customer and Altium’s business      Experience : At least 5 years in Solutions Engineering, Customer Success, Professional Services, or a similar customer-facing strategic role. Relationship Building:  Experience building long-term and successful customer relationships by demonstrating empathy, active listening, and resiliency skills   Subject Matter Expert : Domain expertise and work experience in PCB design or subject matter expertise in functional areas (e.g., ECAD design process, testing, PLM)   Technical Skills : Strong hands-on experience with ECAD software, PLM integrations, and workflow management is essential.   Project Management : Ability to track and coordinate multiple efforts toward a common goal to ensure customer priorities are delivered on time and meet expectations.    Creative Thinker:  Proposes solutions using technical knowledge and experience, building alignment and setting clear expectations with customers on the way forward.   Problem-Solving : Excellent analytical and troubleshooting skills, with the ability to accurately describe technical details of customer issues and how to resolve them   Communication : Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to explain complex technical concepts to different audiences.   Team Player:  Build effective relationships with colleagues across Professional Services, Marketing, Sales, Support, and R&D.   Education : Bachelors/Masters degree in Electrical Engineering, Electronic Engineering, or equivalent degree and experience.   Travel : Willingness to travel, including meeting customers on-site each month.   Language : Fluent in English. Fluency in German is beneficial. About the Role: We are seeking a motivated sales professional to join our sales team supporting a large strategic customer in the semiconductor ecosystem. This is an excellent opportunity for someone with a solid technical foundation in electrical/computer engineering and exposure to customer-facing or sales environments to grow into a high-impact technical sales / account management role.  You will work closely with a major key account to understand their technical needs, position our semiconductor products/solutions, drive design-wins, and support long and complex sales cycles.    Build and maintain relationships with technical and procurement stakeholders at assigned large customer  Qualify customer requirements, present product roadmaps, and conduct technical discussions / demos  Collaborate with internal FAEs, design teams, marketing, and product management to respond to RFQs, create proposals, and secure design-in  Track and report on opportunity pipeline, forecasts, and key account activities  Identify new opportunities within account and support business expansion efforts  Stay current on customer roadmaps, competitive landscape, and emerging trends for the customers end market segment     Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering (EE), Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or closely related field  3–5 years of experience in the semiconductor industry (preferred) or equivalent customer-facing exposure through early-career roles, internships, academic projects, or research in semiconductor or hardware-related domains. Strong technical aptitude with the ability to discuss semiconductor concepts, including processors, SoCs, analog/mixed-signal, power management, RF, memory, and foundry technologies.   Excellent communication and presentation skills (comfortable presenting to engineers and managers)  Self-motivated, organized, and capable of managing multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment. Establish NPI Health & Execution Analytics    Build a comprehensive framework to measure NPI health, execution velocity, readiness, cost/margin, quality, risk, and post-launch performance. Benchmark execution productivity and efficiency across products, programs, functions, resources and sites.    3. Identify root causes and quantify the business and financial impact of operational issues and opportunities. Build the Organization & Drive Business Transformation    Assess the current state and define the target operating model, organization, and transformation roadmap.  Build a high-performing Business & Operational Analytics team with clear interfaces across Business, IT, and Data.  Simplify, standardize, automate, and transform processes using data, analytics, and AI.  Establish scalable tools, standards, and continuous-improvement mechanisms with clear accountability and measurable outcomes.  Partner with senior leaders to turn insights into decisions, actions, and business impact.   5 . Leverage AI & Advanced Analytics    Identify and scale high-value opportunities for AI-enabled operational intelligence.  Develop predictive models for NPI risk, schedule, quality, supply, capacity, cost, and business outcomes.  Deploy AI agents and intelligent workflows to automate data gathering, analysis, issue identification, and performance management.  Move from static dashboards to intelligent, exception-based decision support.  Establish and scale an AI roadmap across PWR.    6. Scale Across PWR    Initially focused on PCP, establish a scalable PWR Performance & Operational Intelligence capability.  Create common standards, metrics, systems, and operating mechanisms across PWR.  Provide leadership with an integrated view of NPI Health | Operational Performance | Productivity | Cost | Risk | Business Impact.    Required   Bachelor’s degree in engineering, Computer Science, Data Science, Business, Operations, or related field; advanced degree preferred.  7–10+ years of progressive experience in business/operational analytics, engineering operations, NPI, transformation, strategy, or related fields. We are looking for an experienced and visionary Functional Safety Architect to define, drive, and govern functional safety concepts for next-generation industrial systems. In this role, you will lead system-level safety architecture across hardware, software, and system boundaries, ensuring compliance with international functional safety standards for industrial, automation, robotics, and energy applications.  You will act as the technical authority for functional safety, bridging customer safety requirements, market regulations, and product engineering. Your work will ensure that our industrial solutions achieve the highest levels of safety, reliability, and regulatory compliance while enabling innovation and time-to-market.  Key Responsibilities   Define and own the system-level functional safety architecture for industrial applications, covering sensors, MCUs/SoCs, power devices, actuators, and communication interfaces.  Translate safety requirements from standards, regulations, and customer use cases into system, hardware, and software safety requirements.  Lead hazard analysis and risk assessment activities (HARA), safety concept development, and safety lifecycle planning.  Define safety mechanisms, diagnostics, redundancy concepts, and fault-handling strategies across HW/SW boundaries.  Ensure alignment with functional safety standards such as IEC 61508, IEC 62061, ISO 13849, and related sector-specific standards.  Drive HW/SW partitioning decisions with a focus on safety integrity, freedom from interference, and fault containment.  Specify and review safety requirements, Safety Requirements Specifications (SRS), safety manuals, and safety case documentation.  Collaborate closely with Product Groups, system architects, hardware, software, and validation teams to ensure end-to-end safety integrity.  Support product definition and roadmaps by assessing safety implications, certification effort, and architectural trade-offs.  Guide and review safety-related design, implementation, verification, and validation activities across the product lifecycle.  Interface with customers, assessors, and certification bodies to support safety assessments, audits, and certifications.  Support customer engagements by explaining safety concepts, assumptions of use, and integration guidelines.  Monitor industry trends, evolving standards, and regulatory requirements, and integrate insights into safety strategies and architectures.  Contribute to reference architectures, application notes, and safety concept reuse across multiple industrial platforms.  Provide functional safety training, mentoring, and technical guidance to internal engineering and application teams.     Master’s or Ph.D. degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Mechatronics, Systems Engineering, or a related field.  8+ years of experience in embedded or industrial system development, with significant responsibility in functional safety.  Proven track record as a Functional Safety Architect, Safety Manager, or Lead Safety Engineer for industrial or automation systems.  Deep understanding of functional safety standards such as IEC 61508, IEC 62061, ISO 13849, and their application to industrial equipment.  Strong experience with safety lifecycle activities including HARA, safety concept definition, safety analysis (FMEA, FMEDA, FTA), and safety validation.  Solid knowledge of embedded systems architecture, microcontrollers/SoCs, real-time software, and industrial communication protocols (e.g., CAN, EtherCAT, PROFINET, Modbus).  Experience defining and assessing safety mechanisms such as diagnostics, watchdogs, redundancy, diversity, and safe-state concepts.  Ability to work cross-functionally and communicate complex safety topics clearly to engineering, business, customers, and assessors.  Strong documentation skills and experience preparing safety-related documentation for internal and external stakeholders. • Experience with cybersecurity and its interaction with functional safety in industrial systems.

エッジAIデバイスから工場設備、データセンター用途まで、産業用プロセッサの適用領域は急速に拡大しています。こうした中、製造業や医療分野などでは、組込み機器を含むシステムのサイバーセキュリティ対策が社会的な課題となっています。そのため、産業向け組込み製品には高度な機能性と高いセキュリティレベルの両立が求められており、オープンソースソフトウェアを活用した機能拡充や、最新のセキュリティ技術を製品へ適用することが重要なテーマとなっています。

【Backgroud】   The application scope of industrial processors is rapidly expanding, ranging from edge AI devices to factory equipment and data center applications. In this context, ensuring cybersecurity for systems that include embedded devices has become a significant societal challenge in sectors such as manufacturing and healthcare.  As a result, embedded products for industrial use are required to achieve both advanced functionality and a high level of security. Expanding product capabilities through the use of open source software and applying the latest security technologies to products have become key priorities.  In this position, you will be responsible not only for device driver development and porting of existing software, but also for addressing emerging industrial standards and advanced security technologies. You will drive these initiatives as part of a global development team, working in collaboration with open source communities.  You will gain hands-on experience in developing open source technologies, particularly Linux-based platforms, as well as security technologies for embedded systems, and delivering these innovations as products to the market.  We are looking for engineers who have a strong interest in these areas and are motivated to contribute to bringing products to market.   【Job Description】   This position is responsible for the design and development of Linux-related software for our industrial high-end processor, RZ series, in collaboration with internal LSI design teams and both domestic and international open source communities.  Based on your skills, experience, and area of expertise, you will primarily be assigned to one or more of the following areas:    Design and development of device drivers for new hardware   Design and development of security features such as hardware-based encryption and secure boot   Design and development of common Linux-related software (e.g., Linux kernel, Trusted Firmware-A, U-Boot, OP-TEE) for high-end processor products, as well as management and maintenance of deliverables as InnerSource assets   Integration and evaluation of open source software for industrial networking functions, such as OPC UA   Technical discussions, proposals, and support with internal and external stakeholders, including open source communities, as well as contribution of patches to those communities   Development and maintenance of build environments using the Yocto Project (e.g., recipe development and maintenance)   Package development for proprietary libraries for Ubuntu and Debian   Management of vulnerability information (CVE: Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures), formulation of patching strategies, and implementation of countermeasures   Planning and management of software maintenance, as well as process improvements and automation to ensure product quality   Technology research, prototyping, and evaluation for next-generation products   *The full details regarding your position scope as well as any future potential changes in work location and job scope will be provided during the interview process.   【MUST】   Experience in embedded software development (approximately 5+ years). As a Customer Staff Application Engineer for Renesas Performance Computing Power Application engineering team, you will be a senior technical contributor and decision maker in new power management applications in the infrastructure server/AI server market. You will engage cross functionally with a diverse team including marketing, software engineering, IC design, and other applications engineering teams to deliver the most innovative power solutions in the server computing market.  Renesas Electronics, a leading global semiconductor company, is rapidly scaling its AI-focused power delivery business. Products include high-performance digital power VRMs, multiphase controllers, Smart Power Stages (SPS), Vertical Power Stages (SPS with integrated capacitors and multiple silicon die), Power Towers (power modules integrating multiple SPS-equivalents with capacitors and inductors), and power MOSFETs.   This senior role provides broad system level solution insight and support.  A broad comprehension of DC/DC power conversion is required including familiarity with digital multiphase PWM controllers. Key responsibilities include:   Travel to customer sites to debug and validate digital multiphase products. Interaction with customers to solve complex problems.  Support marketing efforts by providing detailed solutions matching customer detailed requirements.  Support development efforts by contributing to system validation of new controllers, VPS and SPS products. Work with designers to ensure design teams have the detailed information needed to execute and verify designs.   Develop collateral such as datasheets, performance reports, and application notes to support customer engagement.  Support training of other AE’s and FAE’s to enable broad support and knowledge of the products. Experience & Skills:     Must have minimum of 8 years experience in the power management industry.  Must Have experience with firmware-enabled products and powering large scale application- specific integrated circuit (Central processing unit /Graphics processing unit etc.) in the data center market is required.  Experience with multiphase DC/DC converters powering Intel/AMD/SoC systems.  Mixed-signal Integrated Circuit/System knowledge/experience. Why Altium?   Build the web platform that presents Altium to the world. Our web team owns Altium's public web properties — the main marketing site, documentation portal, customer dashboard, resource centre and localized regional sites — serving high traffic across roughly ten locales. These are some of the contributions you might make to Altium's web platform:    Building headless Next.js / React applications consuming Drupal data over GraphQL    Driving the migration from a Drupal-themed frontend to a modern Next.js stack    Building and maintaining a shared design system on Radix UI, shadcn/ui and Tailwind CSS    Owning the rendering, caching and data-fetching decisions that sit between frontend and CMS    Altium offers the opportunity to shape the frontend architecture of a high-traffic, multi-locale web platform and to move it forward while it keeps running in production    About the Role   Your primary role will be building and evolving the frontend of Altium's web properties, primarily as headless Next.js applications consuming data from Drupal over GraphQL, while keeping the existing Drupal-integrated frontend stable and visually consistent during the ongoing migration. We are hiring for depth in React, Next.js and TypeScript — not for prior Drupal knowledge. Our Drupal frontend layer and deployment specifics are things a strong frontend engineer picks up in a few weeks, and we will support that ramp-up.   A Day in the Life of Our Senior Frontend Developer     Develop features and components in Next.js, React and TypeScript, using the App Router and React Server Components and choosing the right rendering strategy per page    Integrate applications with Drupal via GraphQL and Apollo Client; implement content freshness with ISR and on-demand revalidation    Build and maintain reusable UI components on Radix UI, shadcn/ui and Tailwind CSS, aligned with the design system    Maintain and extend existing Drupal themes (Twig templates, SCSS, Pug-based markup build, Webpack)    Own Core Web Vitals, accessibility and technical SEO for the pages you ship    Write component tests, contribute to the shared Playwright E2E suite and investigate production incidents with Sentry    Participate in code review and contribute to engineering standards and codebase health      Who We're Looking For     4+ years of commercial React experience, including at least 2 years with Next.js in production    Owns a feature end to end — from design handoff through rollout and post-release verification    Traces a production incident from an error report to root cause without hand-holding    Makes technical decisions, states trade-offs explicitly, and updates a position when evidence changes it    Treats visual regressions, accessibility and performance as part of "done", not as follow-up work    Pragmatic about legacy: willing to maintain an existing Drupal-integrated frontend while helping move the platform forward    Reviews others' code constructively and raises the standard of the codebase around them     
 Required Technology Experience     Strong JavaScript and TypeScript (strict mode)    Next.js App Router and React Server Components in production    Client-side GraphQL (Apollo Client or equivalent)    Tailwind CSS; component library and design system principles    Frontend caching: ISR, on-demand revalidation, TTLs and cache invalidation    Core Web Vitals and the tooling to measure and diagnose them    Web accessibility standards    Multi-locale applications    SCSS and at least one template engine (Pug, Twig or similar); Webpack and frontend build pipelines    Git and code review     
 Nice to Have     Drupal theming: templates, theme libraries, integrating markup    Storybook or another component workshop    Image and performance optimization with Next Image and Sharp    Redis and cache strategy / invalidation design    Marketing site instrumentation: GTM, dataLayer, consent management (e.g. OneTrust)    Technical SEO depth: structured data, sitemaps, hreflang across locales

We are seeking a Design Engineer to lead the development of test vehicles supporting our high-current BCD (Bipolar-CMOS-DMOS) and low-voltage GaN power process and product portfolios. This role owns test vehicle definition, circuit and layout design, and characterization planning from concept through silicon bring-up, working closely with process development, product engineering, and applications teams. The ideal candidate has hands-on experience designing power devices and circuits at both the IC and module level, and is fluent in the power topologies these test vehicles are ultimately intended to support.   Key Responsibilities    Define, design, and drive execution of test vehicles (TVs) for high-current BCD and LV GaN process technologies, including device test structures, scaled power stages, and full-function demonstration circuits.  Translate process capability targets and product roadmap requirements into test vehicle architecture and specifications.  Design and simulate power stage circuits (e.g., synchronous buck/boost, multiphase, half-bridge/DrMOS, gate drivers) used to validate device performance under realistic switching and thermal conditions.  Select and characterize power devices (LDMOS, trench MOSFETs, LV GaN HEMTs, Schottky/sync rectifiers) for inclusion in test structures, working with device/process engineering on layout-dependent tradeoffs (RDS(ON), Qg, breakdown voltage, SOA).  Perform IC-level layout and design for test structures, including parasitic-aware layout for switch nodes, current sensing, and gate drive paths.  Extend designs to module/package level as needed — co-design of power stages with packaging, magnetics, and PCB layout for evaluation boards and system-level test vehicles.  Develop test and characterization plans covering DC parametrics, switching performance, efficiency, transient response, and voltage/current stress margins (including switch-node ringing and abs-max validation).  Lead or support silicon bring-up, debug, and correlation of measured results against simulation and design targets.  Collaborate cross-functionally with process integration, reliability, product/applications engineering, and test engineering to close the loop from process split data to product-ready specifications.  Document design methodology, test vehicle results, and characterization data to support technology qualification and product development decisions.     Bachelor's or Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Microelectronics, or related field.  10+ years of hands-on design experience in power semiconductor devices, analog/power ICs, or power electronics.  Strong working knowledge of power conversion topologies (e.g., buck, boost, multiphase/interleaved converters, half-bridge, DrMOS/Intelli-Phase-style architectures) and how topology choices drive device requirements.  Solid understanding of power device physics and tradeoffs across BCD process technologies and GaN (particularly low-voltage GaN HEMTs) — including RDS(ON), switching loss, gate charge, breakdown/avalanche behavior, and thermal characteristics.  Demonstrated experience designing test structures or test chips/vehicles for process technology development (not just product design) — comfortable defining what a process node needs to prove out.  IC-level design and layout experience, including parasitic-sensitive layout practices for high-current switching nodes.  Experience taking designs beyond the die level to module, package, or board level (e.g., power module co-design, evaluation board layout, thermal/electrical co-design).  Proficiency with circuit simulation tools (SPICE or equivalent) and familiarity with device/TCAD simulation concepts.  Ability to interpret and specify absolute maximum ratings, transient voltage tolerance, and protection thresholds (OVP/UVP/OCP/OTP) relevant to power stage reliability.  Strong lab skills: bring-up, debug, and characterization using oscilloscopes, curve tracers, power analyzers, and thermal imaging.    The expected annual pay range for this position is $180K - $230K. This position is also eligible for bonus opportunities. Please note that final offer amount will be dependent on geographic location, applicable experience, and skillset of the candidate. The Staff Power Architect – System Design is responsible for architecture definition, modeling, and technical leadership for PMIC and advanced DC/DC converter products. This role provides architectural ownership and technical leadership from concept through silicon validation. The role works closely with analog design, digital, verification, validation, test, and product engineering teams to ensure alignment of architecture intent, implementation, and verification across multiple programs.   Key Responsibilities   System Architecture & Technical Leadership  - Define and own architectures for PMIC and advanced power converter products across multiple programs.  - Drive architecture trade-offs and define operating modes, startup and shutdown sequencing, and system boundary conditions.  - Lead architecture reviews and remain deeply involved during the design phase to ensure the transition from architecture to design execution is carried out correctly.  - Provide architectural leadership and technical guidance for system-level design decisions across projects.   Modeling & Analysis   - Develop and maintain low-level and system-level models to support architecture decisions and risk reduction, using tools such as Simplis.  - Analyze stability, transient response, fault behavior, and corner cases to support architecture definition and validation.  - Provide model-based insight to support analog design convergence and reduce silicon risk.   Cross-Functional Collaboration   - Collaborate with analog design, digital, verification, validation, test, and applications teams to ensure architecture intent is implemented and verified.  - Participate in design and architecture reviews and technical discussions across multiple programs.  - Provide technical guidance during silicon validation and system-level debug activities.   Documentation & Knowledge Capture   - Create and maintain architecture documentation, design guidelines, and best-practice references.  - Create detailed sub-block specifications that enable design and verification teams to execute implementation and verification activities efficiently.  - Capture lessons learned, root causes, and preventive actions to improve future designs.  - Contribute to internal training, workshops, and technical knowledge-sharing activities.       Required Qualifications   - Strong experience in PMICs, DC/DC converters, or mixed-signal power systems.  - Experience with architecture definition and architectural analysis for power management products.  - Familiarity with modeling tools such as Simplis and Simulink.  - Ability to work across disciplines and influence technical decisions through collaboration and technical credibility.  - Strong written and verbal communication skills for technical documentation and reviews.   Nice to Have   - Experience contributing to advanced power converter programs.  - Familiarity with emerging architectures such as Multi-Level Converter (MLC) topologies.  - Familiarity with multi-rail power systems and power sequencing.  - Experience supporting silicon bring-up, validation, and root-cause analysis.   What Success Looks Like  - Architectures are clearly defined and consistently implemented across projects. As the Senior Principal Platform Architect for UALink Switch Products, you will be the ultimate system-level authority responsible for defining the end-to-end hardware, software, and management architecture of our next-generation AI scale-up network chassis.   In this role, you will look beyond the individual switch silicon to architect the entire platform ecosystem. You will define how multiple UALink switch ASICs interact across backplanes, determine how the system handles multi-kilowatt power delivery and liquid/air cooling orchestration, and architect the platform management stack (BMC/OpenBMC) that allows the switch to seamlessly integrate into massive hyper-scale data centers. You will bridge the gap between silicon engineering, system hardware design, and cloud software orchestration.   1. System & Topology Architecture     Chassis & Rack Definition: Lead the structural, electrical, and logical design of the UALink switch chassis, defining high-speed backplane topologies, cabled scale-up fabrics, and multi-tier switch hierarchies.       Signal & Power Integrity Collaboration: Partner with electrical and SI/PI engineering teams to define parameters for ultra-high-speed SerDes routing across PCBs, flyover cables, and optical components, minimizing bit error rates (BER).       Scale-Up Fabric Optimization: Architect rack-level and row-level topologies that optimize collective communication paths (e.g., All-Reduce, All-to-All) for tens of thousands of interconnected GPUs.     2. Platform Management & Software Infrastructure     Control Plane & BMC Architecture: Architect the end-to-end system management plane. Define how Baseboard Management Controllers (BMCs) monitor, configure, and provision the switch using OpenBMC, Redfish, and PLDM over MCTP.       Boot & Initialization Flows: Establish platform-level boot sequencing, multi-rail power sequencing, and secure multi-node firmware update orchestration.       Platform Security Architecture: Define the hardware security lifecycle, including Platform Firmware Resiliency (NIST SP 800-193), secure enclave integration, and Component Attestation (SPDM).     3. Advanced RAS & Infrastructure Integration     Platform-Level RAS: Architect system-level Reliability, Availability, and Serviceability (RAS) strategies. Define how the platform isolates hardware faults, routes around failed links, handles hot-swapping of fans, power supplies, and switch blades without dropping the AI training cluster.       Thermal & Power Orchestration: Establish dynamic power management and telemetry frameworks to balance the massive transient power draws of next-generation AI workloads against rack-level cooling limits.      Education & Experience     Degree: Master’s or Ph.D. in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field.       Experience: 20+ years of architectural experience in high-performance server platforms, hyper-scale network switches, or data center infrastructure.     Technical Skill Set     System-Level Interconnects: Expert knowledge of high-speed platform fabrics and standards (UALink, NVLink, OAM/UBB, PCIe Gen6/Gen7, CXL, or Ultra Ethernet).       Platform Management Standards: Deep expertise in industry-standard management architectures, including Redfish, IPMI, MCTP, SPDM, and OpenBMC.       Hardware-Software Interface: Thorough understanding of OS/VMM kernels, device drivers, and platform initialization frameworks (UEFI, ACPI).       Data Center Infrastructure: Comprehensive grasp of modern rack architectures (e.g., OCP ORv3), liquid cooling management, and high-density 48V/54V power delivery.     Preferred Attributes (Ways to Stand Out)     Proven track record of delivering a high-volume, multi-million-gate switching or compute platform successfully into top-tier hyper-scale cloud providers (AWS, Azure, GCP, Meta).       Active committee leadership or direct specification contributions within the UALink Consortium, Ultra Ethernet Consortium (UEC), or Open Compute Project (OCP).       Experience architecting systems designed for ultra-high-density accelerator form factors (such as Nvidia Blackwell/Vera Rubin grids or AMD Instinct platforms).      The expected annual pay range for this position is $253,000-315,000K. About the Role & The Reality AI Lab   The Renesas AIoT Center of Excellence in Columbia, MD (formerly Reality AI) is seeking a hands-on Senior Edge AI Applications Engineer to lead our physical lab setup, fabricate sensor prototyping rigs, and deploy low-power machine learning models directly onto microcontrollers (MCUs).  This is a physical, hardware-centric engineering role. You will work at the exact intersection of physical system fabrication, digital signal processing (DSP), C/C++ embedded firmware, and TinyML. You will physically instrument motor control setups, audio arrays, and vibration sensors, collect high-frequency time-series datasets off real physical targets, write DSP feature extraction, and compress ML models to run within kilobytes of RAM on Renesas MCUs.   What This Role IS NOT (Please Read Before Applying)      This IS NOT a Cloud AI, NLP, or LLM Role:  If your primary experience is with LangChain, PySpark, RAG pipelines, or fine-tuning Large Language Models in the cloud, this role is not a fit.     This IS NOT a Remote Software Position:  You will be physically building rigs, soldering, testing hardware with oscilloscopes, and working in our dedicated Columbia, MD lab 100% onsite.     Key Responsibilities      Physical Prototyping & Lab Management:  Hands-on fabrication of physical prototype rigs, custom sensor arrays, and 3D-printed enclosures to capture real-world physical phenomena.     High-Frequency Sensor Data Acquisition:  Instrument physical setups (motors, HVAC, industrial machines, automotive targets) to capture, clean, and preprocess high-frequency time-series datasets (accelerometers, acoustic, electrical, current/voltage).     TinyML & On-Device Model Deployment:  Train, quantize (INT8/FP16), and deploy tiny machine learning models onto microcontrollers (ARM Cortex-M, Renesas RA/RX/RL78) using TensorFlow Lite for Microcontrollers, CMSIS-NN, or eIQ.     Digital Signal Processing (DSP):  Apply DSP feature extraction (FFT, spectrograms, windowing, bandpass filtering, time-domain features) to feed edge inference pipelines.     Embedded Firmware & Driver Development:  Write C/C++ code, bare-metal or RTOS drivers (FreeRTOS, Zephyr), and handle low-level communication (SPI, I2C, UART, CAN, DMA).     Technical Leadership:  Lead junior lab engineers, manage physical lab setups, and collaborate cross-functionally with product and systems teams.       Education:  B.S., M.S., or Ph.D. in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Applied Physics, or a related technical field.    Experience:  3+ years of hands-on experience in embedded systems, hardware prototyping, and deploying edge ML/DSP algorithms onto physical hardware targets.     Hardware & Prototyping Skills:  Proven experience with physical assembly, breadboarding, soldering, 3D printing, schematic reading, and bench debugging using JTAG/SWD, oscilloscopes, and logic analyzers.     Signal Processing (DSP):  Demonstrated fluency in time-series and audio signal processing (spectral analysis, filtering, feature extraction in Python/MATLAB).     Firmware & Embedded C/C++:  Hands-on C/C++ programming for MCUs, RTOS task management, DMA queues, and low-level peripheral drivers.     On-Device ML:  Practical experience with TinyML frameworks (TensorFlow Lite Micro, CMSIS-NN, Edge Impulse) and model quantization/compression for constrained MCU targets. 【背景】 
当部門では、今後の製品競争力を左右するCPUアーキテクチャ設計力の強化が急務となっています。 
システムの中核であるCPUは、性能・電力・コスト・安全性のすべてに影響を与えるため、従来以上に高い視点で全体を見渡せるエンジニアが必要です。 
アーキテクチャ検討において最も重要なのは、システム性能を正しく見極める力です。 
単なる理論値や仕様比較ではなく、実際のユースケースやボトルネックを理解し、「どこに性能を割くべきか」「どこを割り切るべきか」を判断できることが求められます。 
そのためには、プログラムを理解し、自ら作れることが不可欠です。 
ソフトウェアの挙動を理解してこそ、CPU構成やメモリ、バス、割り込み設計といったアーキテクチャ上の意思決定が可能になります。

次世代マイコン／SoC製品に向けたCPUアーキテクチャおよびシステム設計を担当いただきます。

The engineer will analyze specifications, define verification plans, create and execute verification scenarios, and debug RTL issues in close collaboration with design, architecture, and firmware teams.  Daily tasks include running regressions, monitoring coverage metrics, performing root-cause analysis of failures, and contributing to continuous improvement of verification methodologies and automation.  The role may also include mentoring junior engineers, participating in design and verification reviews, and aligning verification activities with project schedules and quality standards. Solid understanding of Computer Architecture, including memory hierarchies, bus protocols, and high-performance compute subsystems.  Proficiency with verification tools and flows (e.g., simulators, waveform viewers, coverage tools, regression management, scripting in Python/Perl/Tcl).  Effective communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to work in cross-functional, multicultural teams.  Experience in semiconductor product development for automotive, industrial, or embedded systems is an advantage  Strong English, availability to support and cooperate with external teams including Business travels.  Experience using AI tools to accelerate code development, debugging, and improvement is an advantage. As a Senior Field Applications Engineer (FAE) you will play a major role in the expansion of our market-leading digital products (MCUs & SoCs), analog and power by providing outstanding application engineering support to our customers. You will also play a key role in the definition of the next generation of Renesas Automotive Products working closely to the customer engineering teams and to Renesas application engineering and marketing teams.  In your new role you will: 
•    Drive the design-in activities of the complete product portfolio in automotive applications such as IVI, ADAS, xEV, Vehicle Controls etc. working with Automotive OEM customers. 
•    Define new products in close cooperation with our innovative customers and our internal technical marketing and applications teams. 
•    Act as a technical interface and consult our customers during the development of all automotive applications with particular focus on OEMs. 
•    Derive customer system requirements and market trends to develop system value propositions together with internal interfaces (Product Marketers, Application Engineers, System Architects). 
•    Build a good understanding of different product architectures and partner ecosystem to suggest/guide customers, to arrive at an optimal system design. 
•    Actively manage projects together with the Sales and Marketing departments to achieve design-in targets for the complete Renesas automotive product portfolio. 
•    Establish and maintain excellent relationships with the customer engineering departments with particular focus on OEMs. 
•    Proactively connect with global cross-functional teams, expand your internal network, and share your experience to drive global business expansion. 
•    Lead technical discussions with System Architects and Application Engineering experts to jointly define application roadmaps and product technical requirements. 
•    Collaborate internally with Application Engineers and Product Marketers and externally with local and global partners to develop documentation (fighting guides, application notes, whitepapers) and system demonstrators combining software and hardware. 
•    Perform measurements in our laboratory within the scope of actual customer projects. 
•    Present Renesas’ technologies, products, and applications in technical seminars. We are seeking a Powertrain Design Engineer to lead the development of test vehicles supporting our high-current BCD (Bipolar-CMOS-DMOS) and low-voltage GaN power process and product portfolios. This role owns test vehicle definition, circuit and layout design, and characterization planning from concept through silicon bring-up, working closely with process development, product engineering, and applications teams. The ideal candidate has hands-on experience designing power devices and circuits at both the IC and module level, and is fluent in the power topologies these test vehicles are ultimately intended to support.   Key Responsibilities    Define, design, and drive execution of test vehicles (TVs) for high-current BCD and LV GaN process technologies, including device test structures, scaled power stages, and full-function demonstration circuits.  Translate process capability targets and product roadmap requirements into test vehicle architecture and specifications.  Design and simulate power stage circuits (e.g., synchronous buck/boost, multiphase, half-bridge/DrMOS, gate drivers) used to validate device performance under realistic switching and thermal conditions.  Select and characterize power devices (LDMOS, trench MOSFETs, LV GaN HEMTs, Schottky/sync rectifiers) for inclusion in test structures, working with device/process engineering on layout-dependent tradeoffs (RDS(ON), Qg, breakdown voltage, SOA).  Perform IC-level layout and design for test structures, including parasitic-aware layout for switch nodes, current sensing, and gate drive paths.  Extend designs to module/package level as needed — co-design of power stages with packaging, magnetics, and PCB layout for evaluation boards and system-level test vehicles.  Develop test and characterization plans covering DC parametrics, switching performance, efficiency, transient response, and voltage/current stress margins (including switch-node ringing and abs-max validation).  Lead or support silicon bring-up, debug, and correlation of measured results against simulation and design targets.  Collaborate cross-functionally with process integration, reliability, product/applications engineering, and test engineering to close the loop from process split data to product-ready specifications.  Document design methodology, test vehicle results, and characterization data to support technology qualification and product development decisions.     Required    Bachelor's or Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Microelectronics, or related field.  10+ years of hands-on design experience in power semiconductor devices, analog/power ICs, or power electronics.  Strong working knowledge of power conversion topologies (e.g., buck, boost, multiphase/interleaved converters, half-bridge, DrMOS/Intelli-Phase-style architectures) and how topology choices drive device requirements.  Solid understanding of power device physics and tradeoffs across BCD process technologies and GaN (particularly low-voltage GaN HEMTs) — including RDS(ON), switching loss, gate charge, breakdown/avalanche behavior, and thermal characteristics.  Demonstrated experience designing test structures or test chips/vehicles for process technology development (not just product design) — comfortable defining what a process node needs to prove out.  IC-level design and layout experience, including parasitic-sensitive layout practices for high-current switching nodes.  Experience taking designs beyond the die level to module, package, or board level (e.g., power module co-design, evaluation board layout, thermal/electrical co-design).  Proficiency with circuit simulation tools (SPICE or equivalent) and familiarity with device/TCAD simulation concepts.  Ability to interpret and specify absolute maximum ratings, transient voltage tolerance, and protection thresholds (OVP/UVP/OCP/OTP) relevant to power stage reliability.  Strong lab skills: bring-up, debug, and characterization using oscilloscopes, curve tracers, power analyzers, and thermal imaging. Some markets you join. This one you help build.  AI compute is outgrowing the ground. As GPU and AI-class systems move into space and other demanding high-reliability settings, the power electronics that feed them have to survive radiation, wide temperature swings, and years of operation with no chance of a service call, at volumes well beyond anything the space industry has produced before. Standard commercial-grade parts cannot meet that bar. Renesas can, and we are opening a new high-reliability (Hi-Rel) growth area to do it: radiation-cognizant power management built on our power portfolio and decades of Hi-Rel heritage.  We are looking for a Staff Business Development Specialist to lead the way into this market. This is a market-creation role, not a territory to maintain. You will find where the real opportunities are, build the customer base from the first conversation, and turn early technical engagements into design wins. You will sit across the table from the GPU and AI-silicon vendors, space-systems primes, and hyperscale operators defining this field, and you will work alongside our product, design, applications, and sales teams to turn those relationships into revenue. If you want your fingerprints on an industry while it is still taking shape, this is that job.  Responsibilities  In this role, you will:  • Identify, pursue, and capture new business in a market Renesas is entering for the first time, from first contact through design-in and production.  • Own senior technical and commercial relationships across the target accounts, from AI-silicon vendors to space-systems primes to hyperscale operators.  • Size the addressable and serviceable market, and build the go-to-market plan that prioritizes accounts, applications, and timing.  • Shape customer requirements early, respond to RFIs and RFPs, and lead proposal development in coordination with product and applications teams.  • Develop pricing and value strategy for radiation-cognizant solutions relative to commodity and fully rad-hard alternatives.  • Run competitive intelligence on incumbent power and Hi-Rel suppliers, and use it to sharpen positioning and roadmap input.  • Support executive reviews and corporate funding proposals with market data, revenue projections, and a defensible business case.  • Work cross-functionally with design, applications, product marketing, and regional sales to align the portfolio with customer needs and to drive design-ins to closure.   • 10 or more years in business development, strategic sales, or product marketing, in semiconductors, power management, aerospace and defense, or high-reliability and space markets.  • Bachelor's degree in electrical engineering or a related field. An MBA is a plus.  • A track record of opening new markets and closing design-ins or partnerships, ideally where the market did not yet exist.  • Direct experience working at, or selling into, GPU and AI-accelerator vendors or hyperscale operators is a major plus.  • The ability to hold technical discussions on power delivery and mixed-signal design with customer engineers, and to translate them into commercial strategy.  • Strong proposal, negotiation, and executive-communication skills.  • Comfort operating in an export-controlled, high-reliability environment.  • Willingness to travel to customers and Renesas sites.  • An independent operator who works effectively across US and Japan-based leadership.   This role offers the chance to build a business from the start inside an established semiconductor company, with the resources of a global portfolio behind it and the impact of a market Renesas is helping to create. We are looking for an experienced and visionary System Architect to serve as Renesas' global technical leader for Drone and UAV applications. This individual will define and drive end-to-end system architectures for next-generation UAV platforms while identifying emerging market opportunities, shaping solution roadmaps, and promoting differentiated semiconductor and software solutions.  You will act as the primary technical authority for Drone & UAV applications, bridging customer requirements, ecosystem needs, aviation regulations, and semiconductor product engineering. Beyond architecture definition, you will help guide solution strategy, ecosystem engagement, reference platform development, and semiconductor adoption across industrial, commercial and defense UAV markets.  Key Responsibilities   Define and own end-to-end system architectures for industrial and/or defense drone and UAV applications, covering flight control, mission computing, sensing, propulsion, power, connectivity, and ground-control interfaces.  Translate customer use cases and mission requirements into system, hardware, software, performance, safety, security, and interface requirements.  Drive HW/SW partitioning across MCUs, MPUs/SoCs, AI accelerators, programmable logic, sensors, connectivity devices, power electronics, and actuators.  Define architectures for flight control, sensor fusion, navigation, positioning, stabilization, autonomous mission execution, obstacle detection, and collision avoidance.  Specify and integrate sensing solutions such as IMUs, GNSS/RTK, cameras, radar, LiDAR, ultrasonic sensors, barometric sensors, and environmental sensors.  Define compute architectures for edge AI, computer vision, visual-inertial odometry, SLAM, object detection, tracking, and autonomous decision-making.  Develop robust communication architectures covering command and control, telemetry, payload data, remote identification, vehicle-to-vehicle links, cloud connectivity, and ground-control systems.  Define power and propulsion architectures, including battery management, power conversion and distribution, motor control, energy optimization, thermal management, and fault monitoring.  Ensure safety, reliability, cybersecurity, redundancy, fault containment, degraded-operation modes, and fail-safe behaviors are designed into the system architecture.  Collaborate closely with Product Groups, system architects, hardware, software, AI, connectivity, power, motor-control, security, and validation teams to deliver cohesive semiconductor-based solutions.  Support product definition and roadmaps by identifying UAV system requirements, technology gaps, architectural trade-offs, and opportunities for differentiated semiconductor and software solutions.  Guide and review system design, implementation, integration, verification, validation, and flight-test activities across the development lifecycle.  Engage with drone OEMs, technology partners, research institutes, and ecosystem providers to understand requirements, support architecture discussions, and accelerate design-in activities.  Support customer engagements by explaining system concepts, design choices, performance trade-offs, integration guidelines, and reference solution capabilities.  Monitor market trends, evolving regulations, emerging technologies, and competitive solutions, and translate insights into application strategies and architectures.  Influence product and technology roadmaps by translating evolving UAV market requirements into strategic semiconductor investment opportunities.  Contribute to reference architectures, evaluation platforms, proofs of concept, application notes, and reusable solution building blocks for multiple UAV platforms.  Provide technical mentoring, design reviews, and domain guidance to internal engineering, application, field, and product teams.     Master’s or Ph.D. degree in Electrical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Computer Engineering, Robotics, Mechatronics, Systems Engineering, or a related field.  8+ years of experience in drone, UAV, aerospace, robotics, autonomous-system, or embedded-system development, with significant responsibility for system architecture and integration.  Systems Engineer in the development of industrial and/or defense drone platforms. Deep understanding of UAV architectures, including flight controllers, mission computers, avionics, propulsion, power systems, payloads, communication links, and ground-control systems.  Strong knowledge of embedded systems, MCUs, MPUs/SoCs, real-time software, embedded Linux, RTOS platforms, and heterogeneous computing architectures.  Strong experience in flight control, estimation, sensor fusion, navigation, GNSS/RTK, perception, autonomy, or other safety- and mission-critical UAV functions.    Nice to Have    Experience with PX4, ArduPilot, ROS 2, MAVLink, DDS, or comparable UAV and robotics software frameworks.  Familiarity with aviation development and safety practices, EASA or FAA UAV regulations, Remote ID, BVLOS operations, and relevant standards such as DO-178C, DO-254, ARP4754A, or ARP4761.  Experience with edge AI, computer vision, SLAM, visual-inertial odometry, radar or LiDAR perception, and AI accelerator platforms.  Background in electric propulsion, motor control, battery management, power conversion, or high-efficiency power electronics for aerial systems.  Experience with cybersecurity, secure communications, GNSS resilience, anti-jamming, or system-level threat analysis.  Knowledge of simulation, model-based systems engineering, software-in-the-loop, hardware-in-the-loop, and digital-twin environments.  Experience supporting third-party assessments, flight approvals, certification, or regulatory compliance activities. ob Description    As a  Mixed-Signal Verification Engineer , you will be responsible for the verification and modeling of mixed-signal power management devices, including PMICs, battery chargers, switching regulators, and related analog IP. You will work closely with design, systems, verification, CAD, and customer teams to drive successful development, integration, and sign-off of complex mixed-signal power chips.   Verification:  Lead chip-level verification of analog and mixed-signal circuits using AMS and DMS methodologies, integrating analog behavioral models with digital RTL and UVM-based environments. Develop verification strategies, drive coverage closure, and support product tapeout milestones.   Modeling:  Create, maintain, and validate behavioral models using SystemVerilog RNM and Verilog-AMS, translating circuit and system requirements into high-performance models suitable for both AMS co-simulation and full-chip DMS verification. Ensure model accuracy through correlation against specifications and schematic references across operating conditions.   Verification Plan Development:  Develop and execute comprehensive verification and modeling plans with full traceability from design requirements through coverage closure and tapeout sign-off. Track verification readiness and proactively identify risks to product schedules.   Debugging:  Own debug and root-cause analysis of mixed-signal verification issues, including failing test cases, model inaccuracies, analog-digital interface problems, convergence issues, and simulation performance bottlenecks. Drive resolution across design, modeling, and verification teams.   Technical Leadership & Collaboration:  Partner with analog and digital designers, system architects, verification engineers, and CAD teams to improve modeling accuracy, simulation efficiency, and verification quality. Participate in architecture and design reviews, influencing design decisions to improve verification effectiveness and reduce project risk.   Design Review & Optimization : Participate in design reviews to evaluate circuit topology and design partitioning from a verification and modeling perspective, recommending architectural choices that simplify behavioral modeling, improve simulation convergence, and reduce verification risk. Support silicon validation and root-cause analysis of complex system-level issues by correlating simulation predictions to bench measurements.   Documentation:  Document verification plans, model validation methodologies, coverage results, and sign-off metrics to ensure clear communication and traceability throughout the product lifecycle.   Customer Interaction:  Interface directly with external customers to present verification status, review coverage results, address technical questions, and ensure verification deliverables meet product and customer requirements.      Education:  B.S. or M.S. in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related field.   Experience:  8-12+ years of experience in mixed-signal verification, AMS/DMS simulation, behavioral modeling, power management IC development, or related semiconductor design activities. Strong experience with switching regulators, battery chargers, PMICs, SystemVerilog, Verilog-AMS, UVM, Cadence Xcelium, Spectre, and mixed-signal verification sign-off methodologies is highly desirable. Experience developing behavioral models and debugging complex analog-digital interactions is a plus.   Communication:  Strong communication, teamwork, and customer-facing skills, with the ability to effectively collaborate across cross-functional engineering teams and present technical information to both internal and external stakeholders.         Renesas is an embedded semiconductor solution provider driven by its Purpose,  To Make Our Lives Easier .
